criteria.text: Given the Command Center, when it is opened, then every tab is reachable and every card drills down one level.
Given sample mode, when any tab is shown, then the sample data is visibly labelled as sample.

Given the Command Center, when any tab renders, then .colaberry/plan.json and .colaberry/progress.json are both committed in this repo and every tab reads its content from them at runtime rather than from hard-coded values.
Given the Command Center, when any tab is shown, then .colaberry/manifest.json is committed in this repo and every tab shows how old that data is and warns when the age exceeds a week.
Trust — no tab shows a number, a connection or a result the project has not actually produced.
Given a new user, when they register, then their account is created with secure password storage.
Given a user, when they attempt to log in with incorrect credentials multiple times, then their account is locked.
Trust: All account and role changes are audited with user and timestamp.

stories.notes: PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA256 password hashing (210k iterations, random salt per hash). Cookie-based session auth with per-account configurable SessionTimeoutMinutes driving server-side ticket expiration (verified by setting an already-elapsed timeout and confirming rejection, not by inspecting cookie headers, since a non-persistent cookie carries no Expires attribute even though the server still enforces it). Account lockout after 5 failed attempts (15 min), using an atomic ExecuteUpdateAsync increment so concurrent failed logins cannot lose an increment to a race - verified with a real concurrent-request test. All account/role-change events (register, login success/failure, lockout, role change) write an audit entry in the same DB transaction as the change itself. Known regression (not fixed, flagged for reviewer): adding the non-nullable Role column broke Alveara.Api.Tests/MigrationUpgradeTests.cs (from ALV-N002), whose "seed on an older migration" test inserts via the current EF model rather than raw SQL matching that older schema. Out of this story's file scope; needs a follow-up fix to MigrationUpgradeTests.cs itself.

criteria.text: Given a user changes their role, when the change is saved, then the action is logged with a timestamp.
Given a user attempts to modify an audit log, when they do not have permission, then the action is denied.
Trust: Audit logs are immutable and protected from unauthorized modification.

stories.notes: Role-change logging (criterion 1) already existed from STORY-001's AccountService/AuditLogEntry work - AccountServiceRoleChangeTests.cs already proved it, reconfirmed here as still passing. New this story: GET /api/auth/audit-log gated on the existing Permission.ViewAuditLog (OfficeManager/Admin allowed, others 403) for read-side permission enforcement, and an AlveraDbContext.SaveChanges guard that throws AuditLogImmutableException on any update/delete of an AuditLogEntry regardless of caller - there is no API endpoint that permits modifying or deleting an entry at all, so 'attempts to modify... denied' holds unconditionally for every role, which is the strongest form of that guarantee. Full backend suite: 184/184 passing.

stories.notes: Demographics and contact details only. REQ-004's family/household clause is not in STORY-003's acceptance and is owned by ALV-003-C01 per the master plan. Verified: backend 420/420, frontend 199/199, mocked browser 40/40, real-backend browser walkthrough 7/7 (axe: 0 critical/serious, light+dark).

criteria.text: Given a provider is available, when an appointment is scheduled, then it is confirmed without conflicts.
Given a provider is double-booked, when a new appointment is attempted, then the system rejects it.
Trust: All scheduling actions are logged with user and timestamp.

stories.notes: Booking only: a provider/operatory conflict, an unavailable provider, an invalid duration and a double booking are refused with a stable code and nothing stored; reschedule, cancel, no-show, patient-overlap and the calendar view are owned by ALV-004-C01. No double booking even when two people book the same slot at once (database application locks per provider and operatory; removing the lock makes the race tests fail). Bookings and refused attempts are audited with user and time. Verified: backend 673/673, frontend 390/390, mocked browser 40/40, real-backend browser walkthrough 10/10 (axe: 0 critical/serious, light+dark), earlier real-backend walkthroughs (patient workspace 14/14, patient registration 7/7, auth 12/12, forms 10/10, Gate A 3/3) still pass.

criteria.text: Given a patient encounter, when documented, then the system records medical and dental history.
Given an encounter note is finalized, when an amendment is needed, then the original is preserved with an addendum.
Trust: All documentation changes are logged with user and timestamp.

stories.notes: Clinical documentation per encounter: structured medical history, dental history, allergies (reaction, severity) and medications (dose, frequency); a section with nothing to report is marked 'reviewed - none reported' so no fact is invented, and finalizing is refused (409, naming the sections) until every section is addressed. A finalized encounter is immutable - refused by the service and by database triggers - and is amended only by an addendum appended beside the untouched original with who and when. Every change, its history row and its PHI-free audit entry are one save, so a failed audit write stores nothing. Reading needs a new ViewClinicalDocumentation permission (dentist, hygienist, assistant, admin) kept separate from ViewPatientRecords so front desk and billing cannot read a medical history; writing needs ManageClinicalNotes. Stale edits are the shared 409; start and addendum are idempotent. Known limits: per-encounter only (no running history, vitals, SOAP notes or templates - ALV-005-C01), addenda are plain text, a finalized encounter cannot be reopened, reads are not audited. See docs/CLINICAL_DOCUMENTATION.md.

criteria.text: Given a tooth is selected, when a condition is recorded, then it is saved with the correct lifecycle state.
Given a completed treatment, when recorded, then the odontogram updates to reflect the change.
Trust: All odontogram updates are logged with user and timestamp.

stories.notes: Interactive odontogram: the Odontogram tab draws the 32 permanent teeth with the state of what is recorded on each as a word (and a border style); selecting a tooth and a surface shows what is recorded by surface; a finding is recorded in the state the clinician chooses (condition and state are chosen, never pre-filled), moved forward Diagnosed, Planned, Completed (or Diagnosed straight to Completed), or withdrawn with a required reason and kept in its history. The stored tooth identity is its FDI/ISO 3950 two-digit string (52 keys, checked by the database); Universal (default), FDI and Palmer are display-only through one mapper that the chart takes as a parameter. Every change, its history version and its PHI-free audit entry are one save, so a failed audit write stores nothing; a stale change is the shared 409; repeats are quiet. Reading needs ViewClinicalDocumentation, writing ManageClinicalNotes. Known limits: no practice-level numbering preference (no story in the master plan owns it; item 22 only specifies a Universal default with an abstraction for FDI/ISO and does not mention Palmer), permanent teeth only on the chart (primary-tooth findings are listed, not drawn), supernumerary teeth and area findings not covered by the key, the six conditions fixed until ALV-006-C01 moves them to a table, no link to diagnosis or treatment plan, reads not audited. See docs/ODONTOGRAM.md.

criteria.text: Given a patient is scheduled, when they check in, then the system updates their status to 'checked-in'.
Given a patient is checked-in, when treatment is completed, then the system updates their status to 'completed'.
Trust: All status changes are logged with timestamps and user IDs.

stories.notes: Patient flow (Scheduled, CheckedIn, InTreatment, Completed) is a separate state from the booking status, so a visit under way still holds its time and no STORY-004 / ALV-004-C01 contract changed. Forward only; InTreatment optional; repeats are no-ops; every move is logged (history + PHI-free audit) in the same save as the change, so a failed log stores nothing. Once checked in, reschedule/cancel/no-show are refused. Known limits: no too-early-to-check-in rule; only ManageAppointments roles can move a patient; no undo. Verified: 767/767 backend, 446/446 frontend, 10/10 real-backend walkthrough, 74 mocked browser.
